steps.text: Place cauliflower in a pot and cover with water; bring to a boil. Cook until tender, about 10 minutes. Drain.
Return drained cauliflower to the pot. Add butter, garlic, salt, and pepper. Mash with a potato masher until smooth and the consistency is similar to mashed potatoes.

raw_recipe.headline: Smashed Cauliflower Side Dish
raw_recipe.description: Smashed cauliflower is prepared just like mashed potatoes but is lower in carbs.
raw_recipe.name: Smashed Cauliflower Side Dish

Return drained cauliflower to the pot. Add butter, garlic, salt, and pepper. Mash with a potato masher until smooth and the consistency is similar to mashed potatoes.

review.reviewBody: Another great variation is to add a couple wedges of laughing cow garlic herb cheese instead of butter . it adds very little fat and calories . If you are on weight watchers as am I am it adds 2 + points per wedge

Wonderful alternative to mashed potatoes. I used a big head of fresh cauliflower as opposed to the frozen packages. I just boiled for 9 minutes and drained. I let mine drain in the colander for about 6-7 minutes and didn't have any problems with watery vegetables. After adding the butter, salt and pepper and garlic right in the pan, I used the immersion blender to blend the cauliflower. It went really well 'San Francisco Pork Chops' and 'Chik-Fil-A® Slaw' both AR recipes.

I make this dish all the time but I do it differently. I use a fresh head of cauliflower and steam it until tender. Instead of butter, I add a 1/4 cup of plain Greek yogurt and a tablespoon of grated Parmesan cheese. I like some peoples idea of adding laughing cow herb cheese as well. I always omit salt unless it absolutely has to be added. The garlic adds a nice touch too. I think frozen cauliflower would lose a lot of the nutrients so I always use fresh ingredients.

Whole family loved it! - I used an extra bag of cauliflower (since there are more of us) and some garlic salt instead of regular salt and it was awesome!...It was a little time consuming only for the fact that I put mine through a food processor and I only have a small one, but totally worth it!

I make this a couple of times a month, however, I do it differently. I drain the cauliflower in a colander, then use a potato masher to get out more water, still in the colander, then transfer the dryer cauliflower to the food processor. I then add salt, 4 oz cream cheese & a handful of mozzarella. I blend until it's creamy & smooth like mashed potatoes. Maybe not the same recipe, but it's a delicious side dish.
PS. I start w/ frozen cauliflower & I use 4 lbs of it at a time, so the 4 oz cream cheese & mozzarella isn't as fattening as it sounds. We eat on it for several days.

I just made this for Dinner tonite! My Husband, 16 yr old son & 13 yr old daughter loved it! Was begging for 2nds!!! I cooked the cauliflower in Homemade Chicken Stock and just mashed it by hand. After reading some reviews, I did drain the cooked Cauliflower onto some paper towels and smashed out as much of the stock water as possible before mashing it. It gave it the consistency of mashed potatoes. Served it with some mushroom brown gravy made from Almond & Coconut flour. The kids had no idea that it was not potatoes until I asked them how it tasted from a scale of 1 - 10; 10 being the best. They rated it an 8 & a 7 before I told them it wasn't Mashed Potatoes, lol.....African-Americans raised on old fashioned Country Cookin' from Scratch!
I used 4 cloves of garlic and roasted it before mixing. It went over VERY well in my household with 3 picky kids.

With my version, I used fresh steamed cauliflower. I added no salt butter, minced garlic, be careful, it can be overwhelming, sour cream and a little milk in my food processor. Pulsed a few seconds, then added chives. Yummy!

This was soooo good! I used fresh cauliflower. Steamed the cauliflower and after draining I used my magic bullet to mash before adding it back to the pot with yogurt, minced garlic, chives and salt and pepper to reheat.

I made this with a fresh head of cauliflower. After the water came to a boil, I threw in a few peeled whole cloves of garlic. I drained the cauliflower in a colander and removed the garlic cloves and smashed in the pot and then returned the cauliflower to the pot. I only used about 2-3 tbsps of butter and sprinkled some garlic powder - tasted just like garlic mashed potatoes!

This was a great start..... I used a half head of fresh cauliflower (there is only 2 of us), steamed it until very soft, then I drained it and saved the steaming water for something else another day. Next I returned it to the same pan and mashed it with a potato masher. Then I added 4 ounces of cream cheese and mashed it all together, no salt and no butter. They were positively delicious!! I made this to go along with some organic skinless chicken breasts, that I stuffed with fresh spinach, feta cheese, sour cream and fresh garlic. I also made twice baked yams with chopped pecans and honey. This was a wonderful meal for us!!!
I made this but added shredded italian cheese blend and it was so good my husband and I ate all of it. Will be making again.
Cook your rozen cauliflower in the microwave, for about 8 -10 minutes.
pretty bland. next time I'll add some green onion and cheddar cheese

I made exactly to the recipe and tasted it but didn't it. I added a 1/4 cup of sour cream and a spice blend from a local shop which made it much better. I will try again but only make a half recipe and try the suggestion of using laughing cow wedges.

Too watery... not the same consistency as mashed potatoes.
Fooled my whole family and they all loved it despite “hating” cauliflower
I used the laughing cow cheese in place of the butter. The taste was good but needed a little something more as a binder. But overall a good option!

Great side dish. Served it with a pork roast, gravy, asparagus. Worked well. My guest thought it wsa mashed potatoes and we had a great laugh after his first bite. After the initial shock as he was expecting good ole' mashed potatoes -- he admitted he liked it a lot and wanted the recipe and instructions.
